title: Bank strike on September 11: Banking services likely to be hit as unions push for 5-day week, PLI rollback- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Bank strike on September 11: Banking services may be affected as unions demand a 5-day banking week and changes to the PLI scheme. Check strike dates and impact.   September 10, 2026 / 13:21 IST             Banking services across India are likely to be affected on Friday, September 11, as bank employee and officer unions have called a nationwide strike over the implementation of a five-day banking week and changes to the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), an umbrella body representing major bank employee and officer unions, has announced a series of strikes as it presses the government and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) to address the demands. The next nationwide strike is scheduled for September 11, followed by a three-day strike from September 28 to 30. If the issues remain unresolved, the unions have threatened an indefinite strike from October 26. WHY ARE BANK EMPLOYEES DEMANDING A 5-DAY WORKING WEEK? The demand for a five-day banking week is not new. The UFBU has pointed to the 12th Bipartite Settlement and 9th Joint Note signed in March 2024, under which the IBA agreed to introduce five-day banking by increasing the daily working hours from Monday to Friday. The proposal would effectively mean that bank branches remain closed on Saturdays and Sundays, with the additional working time on weekdays making up for the change. According to the unions, the proposal has been pending with the government for more than two years despite being recommended by the IBA. WHAT IS THE DISPUTE OVER PLI? The second major issue is the revised Performance Linked Incentive scheme. The unions say they had agreed with the IBA that PLI would be linked to the overall performance of a bank and would follow a uniform structure for employees and officers up to Scale VII. However, the UFBU has objected to a revised framework under which officers in Scale IV and above could receive PLI of up to 365 days of basic pay based on individual performance, while workmen employees and officers up to Scale III would be eligible for a maximum of 15 days of basic pay plus dearness allowance. The unions have described the structure as discriminatory and have called for the revised PLI framework to be withdrawn and discussed through bilateral negotiations. WILL BANKS IN INDIA REMAIN CLOSED ON SEPTEMBER 11? With the strike called by the unions, physical banking operations at participating branches are expected to be disrupted on September 11. However, customers may still be able to access digital banking channels such as internet banking, mobile banking, ATMs and other automated services, although the availability of individual services can vary by bank. The September 11 strike is the first of the latest planned nationwide actions. The UFBU has also announced strikes from September 28 to 30, followed by an indefinite strike from October 26 if its demands are not resolved. Bank strike on September 11: Banking services may be affected as unions demand a 5-day banking week and changes to the PLI scheme. Check strike dates and impact.

September 10, 2026 / 13:21 IST

Banking services across India are likely to be affected on Friday, September 11, as bank employee and officer unions have called a nationwide strike over the implementation of a five-day banking week and changes to the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.

The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), an umbrella body representing major bank employee and officer unions, has announced a series of strikes as it presses the government and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) to address the demands. The next nationwide strike is scheduled for September 11, followed by a three-day strike from September 28 to 30. If the issues remain unresolved, the unions have threatened an indefinite strike from October 26.

WHY ARE BANK EMPLOYEES DEMANDING A 5-DAY WORKING WEEK?

The demand for a five-day banking week is not new.

The UFBU has pointed to the 12th Bipartite Settlement and 9th Joint Note signed in March 2024, under which the IBA agreed to introduce five-day banking by increasing the daily working hours from Monday to Friday.

The proposal would effectively mean that bank branches remain closed on Saturdays and Sundays, with the additional working time on weekdays making up for the change.

According to the unions, the proposal has been pending with the government for more than two years despite being recommended by the IBA.

WHAT IS THE DISPUTE OVER PLI?

The second major issue is the revised Performance Linked Incentive scheme.

The unions say they had agreed with the IBA that PLI would be linked to the overall performance of a bank and would follow a uniform structure for employees and officers up to Scale VII.

However, the UFBU has objected to a revised framework under which officers in Scale IV and above could receive PLI of up to 365 days of basic pay based on individual performance, while workmen employees and officers up to Scale III would be eligible for a maximum of 15 days of basic pay plus dearness allowance.

The unions have described the structure as discriminatory and have called for the revised PLI framework to be withdrawn and discussed through bilateral negotiations.

WILL BANKS IN INDIA REMAIN CLOSED ON SEPTEMBER 11?

With the strike called by the unions, physical banking operations at participating branches are expected to be disrupted on September 11.

However, customers may still be able to access digital banking channels such as internet banking, mobile banking, ATMs and other automated services, although the availability of individual services can vary by bank.

The September 11 strike is the first of the latest planned nationwide actions. The UFBU has also announced strikes from September 28 to 30, followed by an indefinite strike from October 26 if its demands are not resolved.
